doc.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: White Dixieland dominance and the Preservation Hall Jazz Band
summary: They criticize festivals saturated with Dixieland played mostly by white musicians, with Preservation Hall as an exception.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I have to comment on your comment about Dixieland and that the groups that are playing Dixieland now, something has changed from the original, I mean which of course will happen, but it seems to be to me a little bombastic most of the time, and overdone.

Well I think they saturate you with it. It isn’t like you can go to a concert and hear one or two Dixieland tunes. You go to one of these kinds of festivals, and that’s all you hear. I don’t mind that if you’re going to go to a Bix Beiderbecke memorial concert, then you can hear all that kind of music. On the other hand if I go to a jazz festival quote unquote, I don’t want it to be all of anything because jazz is too broad a spectrum. And I do think that the African Americans who have moved away from that kind of music for one reason or another and some of those reasons are very good, some of them I may not agree with. But the fact is they’ve moved away from that music, which is traditionally and historically their music. And now to see that kind of music only played by white musicians and has a bit of a racial overtone to it, that turns me off.

I agree. And when I look at the folks that are playing/producing for lack of a better term classic jazz now, it seems to be almost all white musicians on the labels I see. And I wonder why that is. But I sound like I’m complaining too much.

Well I saw the Preservation Hall Jazz Band just recently. And interesting that that band is not an example of what we’re talking about. Either what you or I have said, the exception is the Preservation Hall Jazz Band. Number one they’re still mostly African Americans in the band and number two, they have both the very, very old and the very, very young — some wonderful young players, African American, are in that band. So I’m glad that there’s one exception.
